operations.summary: Old release updates only legacy_name by id.
New release updates only display_name by id.
Selects ids where display_name IS NULL then copies legacy_name to display_name one row per transaction without IS NULL guard.

conflicts.risk_explanation: Backfill SELECTs rows WHERE display_name IS NULL in one transaction then UPDATEs display_name unconditionally by id in later transactions without rechecking IS NULL. A concurrent app_v2 write to the same id between SELECT and UPDATE is clobbered (lost update).

Backfill copies legacy_name to display_name across separate transactions (TOCTOU). An app_v1 update to legacy_name between SELECT batch and per-row UPDATE causes backfill to write a stale value. app_v1 also never maintains display_name, so any post-backfill legacy write leaves display_name permanently stale/diverged.

tests.name: backfill_overwrites_concurrent_display_write
tests.rationale: Same-row write-write on display_name. Both serial orders end with v2 value (v2-after-backfill overwrites; v2-before-backfill makes SELECT skip the row). Interleaving SELECT-before-v2 with unconditional UPDATE-after-v2 resurrects stale legacy value and loses v2. Second NULL row keeps SELECT non-empty so the bound UPDATE is always feasible.

invariants.description: Concurrent v2 display value must survive backfill; guarded backfill would leave it intact in all orders.

tests.name: backfill_copies_stale_legacy_value
tests.rationale: Backfill reads legacy_name then writes display_name in a later transaction while v1 only writes legacy_name. If v1 commits between SELECT and UPDATE, backfill copies stale orig-name; if v1 commits after backfill, display stays stale. Correct rollout (v1 dual-write plus atomic/guarded backfill) would converge display to v1-new-name in every order.

invariants.description: With dual-write/atomic copy, display must equal final legacy v1-new-name in all orders.

tests.name: old_and_new_writes_diverge_columns
tests.rationale: v1 writes only legacy_name and v2 writes only display_name with no trigger/dual-write. Concurrent or serial updates with different logical values leave the row split-brained (legacy=name-from-v1, display=name-from-v2). Correct expand-migrate-contract code would keep them equal.

invariants.description: Synced releases would keep both name columns equal via last-writer-wins.
